nodes.title: SG-6.4.1 · Add rejectExecution to the API client
nodes.body:
Context: game/frontend/src/api/client.ts exports approveExecution and retryExecution, which POST to /api/v1/admin/executions/{id}/approve and /retry through adminRequest. There is no rejectExecution. Desired behavior: add rejectExecution(token, id), which POSTs to /api/v1/admin/executions/{id}/reject with the Bearer token. Expected result: later UI work can call it. Why: SG-6.4 needs a Reject action in AdminApp.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a token and an execution id, when rejectExecution is called, then fetch is sent POST to /api/v1/admin/executions/{id}/reject with an Authorization Bearer header.
- Given the server answers 401, when rejectExecution is called, then the promise rejects with an ApiError whose status is 401.


## Scope
- In scope: rejectExecution function in game/frontend/src/api/client.ts
- Out of scope: Backend reject route and handler
- Out of scope: ExecutionPanel Reject button
- Out of scope: AdminApp wiring
- Preserve: approveExecution, retryExecution and listExecutions behavior
- Preserve: adminRequest and readJSON


## Technical constraints
- Use adminRequest like approveExecution and retryExecution do.
- Return Promise<ExecutionInfo>.
- Encode the id with encodeURIComponent.


## Definition of done
- rejectExecution is exported from client.ts and the frontend type-checks.


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · rejectExecution client call POSTs to the admin reject endpoint
nodes.body:
Context: approveExecution and retryExecution wrap adminRequest in client.ts (about L92-L105). Desired behavior: a sibling rejectExecution does the same for the reject path. Expected result: callers get the ExecutionInfo the server returns, or an ApiError on failure. Why: the admin UI needs a client call before it can offer Reject.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given token 'tok' and id 'exec-1', when rejectExecution is called, then fetch receives URL /api/v1/admin/executions/exec-1/reject with method POST and header Authorization 'Bearer tok'.
- Given a 200 response with an execution JSON body, when rejectExecution resolves, then it returns that execution.
- Given a 401 response, when rejectExecution is called, then it rejects with ApiError status 401.


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/api/client.ts
- Out of scope: backend changes
- Out of scope: UI changes
- Preserve: existing client exports


## Technical constraints
- Mirror approveExecution exactly except for the path suffix.


## Definition of done
- Function exported and covered by unit tests.


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Verify: rejectExecution unit tests with mocked fetch
nodes.body:
Add tests in game/frontend/tests/executions.test.ts using a stubbed global fetch. The fixture is executionFixture from tests/fixtures/api.ts, which mirrors execution.Execution in backend/internal/execution/execution.go.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given token 'tok' and id 'exec-1', when rejectExecution runs, then fetch is called once with URL /api/v1/admin/executions/exec-1/reject, method POST and Bearer tok.
- Given a 200 response carrying executionFixture, when it resolves, then the result equals executionFixture.
- Given a 401 response, when it runs, then it rejects with ApiError status 401.


## Scope
- In scope: tests/executions.test.ts
- Out of scope: real network or server
- Preserve: existing tests in the file

- Code path: `game/frontend/tests/executions.test.ts`


## Dependencies
